title: Schrödinger operators and spectral types
summary: Measure-theoretic spectral types (Lebesgue decomposition of vector spectral measures, sigma_ac/sc/pp, the interval criterion, min-max below the essential spectrum, wave operators, Kato-Rosenblum) for arbitrary self-adjoint operators; lower bounds and cores under bounded and Kato-Rellich perturbations; the Laplace-Beltrami operator of a Riemannian manifold from C_c^infinity to its self-adjoint closure on complete manifolds (Gaffney-Chernoff-Strichartz) with its spectral vocabulary, compact case, bounded potentials and the cusp threshold 1/4; the free Laplacian on H^2(R^d) and -Delta + V for real bounded V with sigma_ess = [0, infinity) when V vanishes at infinity, and quasi-periodic potentials.

targets.name: ProjValMeasure.diag_laws
targets.statement: For self-adjoint A on a complex Hilbert space H with spectral PVM P_A and mu_f = P_A.diag f: mu_{P_A(B) f} = mu_f.restrict B for Borel B; mu_{g(A) f} = mu_f.withDensity |g|^2 for bounded Borel g; if <f, P_A(B) h> = 0 for all Borel B then mu_{f+h} = mu_f + mu_h; for unitary U and A' = U A U^{-1}, P_{A'}(B) = U P_A(B) U^{-1} and mu^{A'}_{Uf} = mu^A_f.
hypotheses: U : H -> H' linear isometric equivalence

tests.name: diag2_calculus
tests.statement: A = diag(1,2), f = (1,i): mu_f = delta_1 + delta_2; g = 3*1_{2}: mu_{g(A)f} = 9 delta_2 (|g| instead of |g|^2 gives 3 delta_2).

tests.name: orthogonality_needed
tests.statement: A = 0 on C^2, f = h = (1,0): mu_{f+h} = 4 delta_0 /= 2 delta_0 = mu_f + mu_h, and <f, P(R) h> = 1.

tests.name: zero_space
tests.statement: On the zero Hilbert space every mu_f is the zero measure and mu_f(R) = ||f||^2 = 0.

targets.name: diag_typeProjection_eq_lebesgueDecomposition
targets.statement: With P_pp, P_ac, P_sc the projections onto the UO-C03 subspaces: for every f, mu_f = mu_{P_ac f} + mu_{P_sc f} + mu_{P_pp f}; mu_{P_ac f} = volume.withDensity (mu_f.rnDeriv volume); mu_{P_sc f} + mu_{P_pp f} = mu_f.singularPart volume; mu_{P_pp f} = mu_f.restrict {x | mu_f {x} > 0}; mu_{P_sc f} is the restriction of mu_f.singularPart volume to the complement of the atoms of mu_f.
hypotheses: A self-adjoint on a complex Hilbert space (no separability)

tests.name: orientation_witness
tests.statement: A = M_x on L^2[0,1], f = sqrt2*1: mu_f = 2 Leb|[0,1] = mu_{P_ac f}, while mu_f.withDensity(mu_f.rnDeriv Leb) = 4 Leb|[0,1].

tests.name: cantor
tests.statement: A = multiplication by x on L^2([0,1], Cantor measure c): H_sc = H, singular part of mu_1 is c, atomless.

targets.name: spectralPVM_reducedRestriction
targets.statement: If U is a closed subspace of H whose orthogonal projection Q commutes with every P_A(B), then U reduces A, A|_U is self-adjoint, its spectral PVM is the compression B -> P_A(B)|_U, mu^{A|_U}_u = mu^A_u for u in U, and sigma(A|_U) = {lambda : P_A((lambda-eps, lambda+eps)) Q /= 0 for every eps > 0}.
hypotheses: Q P_A(B) = P_A(B) Q for all Borel B

tests.name: diag3
tests.statement: A = diag(1,2,3), U = span(e1,e3): sigma(A|_U) = {1,3}; unrestricted P_A would give {1,2,3}.

tests.name: zero_subspace
tests.statement: U = 0: sigma(A|_U) is empty.

tests.name: whole_space
tests.statement: U = H: the compression is P_A and sigma(A|_U) = sigma(A).

targets.name: acSpectrum
targets.statement: sigma_ac(A) := spectrum of the reduced restriction A_ac of A to H_ac(A) (UO-C03); sigma_sc(A), sigma_pp(A) likewise with H_sc, H_pp.
hypotheses: A self-adjoint on a complex Hilbert space

api.name: acSpectrum_subset_spectrum
api.statement: sigma_xx(A) is a closed subset of sigma(A).

api.name: acSpectrum_eq_empty_iff
api.statement: sigma_xx(A) is empty iff H_xx(A) = 0.

api.name: acSpectrum_unitary
api.statement: sigma_xx(U A U^{-1}) = sigma_xx(A) for unitary U.

api.name: spectrum_eq_union_parts
api.statement: sigma(A) = sigma_ac(A) U sigma_sc(A) U sigma_pp(A) (UO-C03).

tests.name: multiplier
tests.statement: A = M_x on L^2[0,1]: sigma_ac = [0,1], sigma_sc = sigma_pp = empty.

tests.name: rational_diagonal
tests.statement: A = diag(q_n), q_n enumerating Q cap [0,1]: sigma_pp = [0,1], sigma_ac = empty; the wrong model sigma(A) minus sigma_p(A) gives [0,1] minus Q.

tests.name: overlap
tests.statement: A = M_x (+) diag(q_n): sigma_ac = sigma_pp = [0,1], the union is not disjoint.

tests.name: zero_space
tests.statement: Zero Hilbert space: all three parts are empty.

targets.name: essentialClosure
targets.statement: For Borel N subset R, N^ess := {lambda : Leb((lambda-eps, lambda+eps) cap N) > 0 for every eps > 0}.

api.name: isClosed_essentialClosure
api.statement: N^ess is closed.

api.name: essentialClosure_subset_closure
api.statement: N^ess is contained in closure N.

api.name: essentialClosure_congr_ae
api.statement: N =ae M implies N^ess = M^ess.

tests.name: rationals
tests.statement: Q^ess = empty while closure Q = R.

tests.name: open_interval
tests.statement: (0,1)^ess = [0,1]: endpoints kept.

targets.name: IsMaximalSpectralVector
targets.statement: psi is a maximal spectral vector of A when mu_f << mu_psi for every f in H.

api.name: IsMaximalSpectralVector.typeProjection
api.statement: If psi is maximal then mu_{P_xx psi} is a maximal spectral measure of A_xx.

api.name: exists_maximalSpectralVector_of_separable
api.statement: On a separable H a maximal spectral vector exists (SA-B85 countable cyclic decomposition).

tests.name: diag2
tests.statement: A = diag(1,2): (1,1) maximal, (1,0) not (mu_{(0,1)} = delta_2).

tests.name: zero_operator
tests.statement: A = 0 on C^2: every nonzero vector is maximal although not cyclic.

tests.name: nonseparable
tests.statement: Coordinate operator on l^2(R): no maximal spectral vector.

targets.name: mem_acSpectrum_iff
targets.statement: lambda in sigma_ac(A) iff for every eps > 0 some f has (volume.withDensity (mu_f.rnDeriv volume))((lambda-eps,lambda+eps)) > 0, iff one f has this for every eps; likewise for sigma_sc and sigma_pp with the continuous singular and atomic parts. sigma_ac(A) has no isolated points. If psi is a maximal spectral vector and h is a Borel version of mu_psi.rnDeriv volume, sigma_ac(A) = {h > 0}^ess. On separable H a maximal spectral vector exists.
hypotheses: A self-adjoint on a complex Hilbert space
separability only for the last clause

tests.name: no_isolated
tests.statement: A = M_x on L^2([0,1]) (+) diag(2): sigma_ac = [0,1], the isolated 2 lies in sigma_pp only.

targets.name: Icc_subset_acSpectrum_iff
targets.statement: For a < b: [a,b] subset sigma_ac(A) iff every nonempty open J subset (a,b) has some f with (mu_f)_ac(J) > 0; in particular if some f has mu_f.rnDeriv volume > 0 a.e. on [a,b]; and sigma_ac(A) cap (a,b) = empty iff (mu_f)_ac((a,b)) = 0 for all f.

tests.name: a_eq_b
tests.statement: a = b is excluded: (a,a) empty makes the right side vacuous while {a} subset sigma_ac(0) fails.

tests.name: two_intervals
tests.statement: M_x on L^2([0,1] U [2,3]): [0,1] subset sigma_ac, sigma_ac cap (1,2) empty.

tests.name: fat_cantor
tests.statement: M_x on L^2(K), K fat Cantor: sigma_ac = K^ess contains no interval.

targets.name: minMaxValue
targets.statement: For A self-adjoint and bounded below and n >= 1, mu_n(A) := sup over phi_1..phi_{n-1} of inf {<psi, A psi> : psi in dom A, ||psi|| = 1, psi orthogonal to phi_i}, valued in R U {+infinity}.

api.name: minMaxValue_mono
api.statement: n -> mu_n(A) is nondecreasing.

api.name: minMaxValue_core
api.statement: The same values arise on any core and on the form domain.

api.name: minMaxValue_le_of_le
api.statement: If A <= B in the form order (Q(B) subset Q(A) and q_A(psi) <= q_B(psi) for psi in Q(B), form domains of UO-D06), then mu_n(A) <= mu_n(B) for every n.

tests.name: diag135
tests.statement: A = diag(1,3,5): mu_1..mu_3 = 1,3,5 and mu_4 = +infinity (a real junk convention would report 0).

tests.name: multiplier
tests.statement: A = M_x on L^2[0,1]: mu_n = 0 = inf sigma_ess for all n.

tests.name: form_order
tests.statement: diag(1,3) <= diag(2,4): mu_1 = 1 <= 2, mu_2 = 3 <= 4. On (0,1) Neumann N <= Dirichlet D in the form order (H^1_0 subset H^1, same form): mu_n(N) = (n-1)^2 pi^2 <= n^2 pi^2 = mu_n(D); comparing forms on the common domain alone would also give D <= N, yet mu_1(D) = pi^2 > 0 = mu_1(N).

targets.name: minMaxValue_eq
targets.statement: If A has at least n eigenvalues below inf sigma_ess(A) counted with multiplicity, mu_n(A) is the n-th; otherwise mu_n(A) = inf sigma_ess(A) (+infinity if empty). For lambda < inf sigma_ess(A), dim ran P_A((-infinity, lambda)) = #{n : mu_n(A) < lambda}.

targets.name: waveOperator
targets.statement: For self-adjoint H_1, H_2 and a sign, D_pm(H_2,H_1) := {psi : e^{itH_2} e^{-itH_1} psi converges as t -> pm infinity}, and Omega_pm psi is the limit.
hypotheses: H_1, H_2 self-adjoint on the same complex Hilbert space

api.name: waveOperator_isometry
api.statement: D_pm and Omega_pm(D_pm) are closed and Omega_pm is unitary between them.

api.name: waveOperator_intertwines
api.statement: Omega_pm e^{-isH_1} = e^{-isH_2} Omega_pm on D_pm; the subspaces reduce H_1, H_2.

api.name: waveOperator_chain
api.statement: Omega_pm(H_3,H_1) = Omega_pm(H_3,H_2) Omega_pm(H_2,H_1) where defined.

tests.name: identity
tests.statement: H_1 = H_2: D = H, Omega = 1.

tests.name: scalar_shift
tests.statement: H_1 = 0, H_2 = 1 on C: e^{it} psi converges only for psi = 0.

tests.name: bounded_not_trace_class
tests.statement: H_1 = M_x on L^2(R), H_2 = H_1 + c: e^{itc} has no limit, D = 0 although sigma_ac equal.

targets.name: waveOperator_properties
targets.statement: Teschl Lemma 12.1 and Theorem 12.2: closedness, unitarity, reduction, intertwining Omega H_1 psi = H_2 Omega psi on D cap dom H_1, chain rule; if H_ac(H_1) subset D_pm then Omega_pm(H_ac(H_1)) subset H_ac(H_2).

targets.name: IsDensityBounded
targets.statement: x in H_ac(H) is density-bounded with constant m when mu_x.rnDeriv volume <= m^2 almost everywhere.

api.name: dense_densityBounded
api.statement: Density-bounded vectors are dense in H_ac(H): P_H({h <= m^2}) x -> x.

api.name: densityBounded_mono
api.statement: Constant m implies constant m' for m <= m'.

tests.name: multiplier
tests.statement: For H = M_lambda on L^2(R), x is density-bounded iff x in L^infinity cap L^2.

tests.name: unbounded_density
tests.statement: x = |lambda|^{-1/4} 1_{[-1,1]} lies in H_ac with density |lambda|^{-1/2}, not density-bounded.

tests.name: no_ac_part
tests.statement: If H_ac(H) = 0 the only density-bounded vector is 0.

targets.name: rosenblum_lemma
targets.statement: For density-bounded x with constant m and Hilbert-Schmidt C: integral over R of ||C e^{-itH} x||^2 dt <= 2 pi m^2 ||C||_HS^2. For bounded self-adjoint trace-class V, |V|^{1/2} is Hilbert-Schmidt with ||V|^{1/2}||_HS^2 = nuclearENorm V.
hypotheses: V bounded self-adjoint, nuclearENorm V /= top

tests.name: equality_case
tests.statement: H = M_lambda, x = m 1_{[0,1]}, C = <phi,.>phi with phi unit supported in [0,1]: the integral equals 2 pi m^2.

tests.name: square_root
tests.statement: V = diag((-1)^{n+1}/n^2): |V|^{1/2} = diag(1/n), HS energy pi^2/6 = nuclear gauge.

targets.name: kato_rosenblum
targets.statement: If H_1 is self-adjoint and V bounded self-adjoint trace class, H_2 = H_1 + V on dom H_1, then Omega_pm(H_2,H_1) and Omega_pm(H_1,H_2) exist on the absolutely continuous subspaces and are complete; the compressed wave operator W_pm(H_2,H_1) := Omega_pm(H_2,H_1) P_ac(H_1) (Kato's strong limit of e^{itH_2} e^{-itH_1} P_ac(H_1)) is a partial isometry with initial space H_ac(H_1) and final space H_ac(H_2); W_pm(H_2,H_1)* = W_pm(H_1,H_2); H_2 P_ac(H_2) = W_pm H_1 P_ac(H_1) W_pm*; hence (H_1)_ac and (H_2)_ac are unitarily equivalent and sigma_ac(H_1) = sigma_ac(H_2). Omega_pm itself is the unrestricted limit of 1.7a and need not vanish off H_ac(H_1).
hypotheses: H_1 self-adjoint on a complex Hilbert space
V bounded, self-adjoint, nuclearENorm V /= top

locator.where: line 21-35 (Theorem 1); rs3 SXI.3 Theorems XI.7-XI.8; rosenblum57 Theorem 1.6 line 70-72

tests.name: zero_perturbation
tests.statement: V = 0: W_pm = P_ac(H_1) while Omega_pm = 1 on D_pm = H; for H_1 = diag(1,2) on C^2, W_pm = 0 (initial and final space 0) although Omega_pm = 1, so the theorem is false for Omega_pm itself; for H_1 = M_x on L^2(R), W_pm = Omega_pm = 1.

tests.name: rank_one
tests.statement: H_1 = M_x on L^2(R), V rank one: sigma_ac(H_2) = R.

tests.name: pure_point
tests.statement: H_1 = diag(1/n^2), V = -diag(1/n^2): H_ac(H_1) = H_ac(H_2) = 0, W_pm = 0, and D_pm = 0 since no coordinate e^{-it/n^2} c_n with c_n /= 0 converges; V = -diag(1/n) is compact but not trace class and excluded.

targets.name: spectrumBottom
targets.statement: For A self-adjoint and bounded below on a nonzero complex Hilbert space, lambda_0(A) := inf sigma(A) (real spectrum).

api.name: spectrumBottom_mem
api.statement: lambda_0(A) in sigma(A).

api.name: spectrumBottom_add_const
api.statement: lambda_0(A + c) = lambda_0(A) + c.

api.name: spectrumBottom_unitary
api.statement: lambda_0(U A U^{-1}) = lambda_0(A).

tests.name: free_shift
tests.statement: A = H_0 + c: lambda_0 = c, not an eigenvalue.

tests.name: zero_space
tests.statement: On the zero space sigma = empty and inf is junk; H nonzero is required.

tests.name: unbounded_below
tests.statement: A = M_x on L^2(R): sigma = R, definition does not apply.

targets.name: spectrum_subset_Ici_iff_formBound
targets.statement: For gamma real: gamma ||x||^2 <= <x, A x> on dom A iff sigma(A) subset [gamma, infinity) iff P_A((-infinity, gamma)) = 0; hence lambda_0(A) = inf of the Rayleigh quotient over dom A, over any core, or over the form domain.

targets.name: boundedPerturbation_core_bottom
targets.statement: For A self-adjoint and V bounded self-adjoint: every core of A is a core of A + V; if A is bounded below on nonzero H then lambda_0(A) + inf sigma(V) <= lambda_0(A + V) <= lambda_0(A) + sup sigma(V), in particular |lambda_0(A + V) - lambda_0(A)| <= ||V||.
hypotheses: H nonzero for the bottom statements

tests.name: diag2
tests.statement: A = diag(0,1), V = diag(1,-1): A + V = diag(1,0), lambda_0 = 0 in [-1, 1].

tests.name: constant
tests.statement: V = c: equality in both bounds.

targets.name: katoRellich_lowerBound_core
targets.statement: Let A be self-adjoint with gamma ||x||^2 <= <x, A x>, V symmetric with dom A <= dom V and ||V x|| <= a ||x|| + b ||A x|| (a >= 0, 0 <= b < 1). Then A + V (self-adjoint by IsSelfAdjoint.add_of_isRelativelyBounded) has every core of A as a core and is bounded below by gamma - max(a/(1-b), a + b|gamma|).
hypotheses: A self-adjoint, bounded below by gamma

locator.where: line 5683-5720 (Lemma 6.3, Theorem 6.4); kato76 Ch. V S4.1 Theorem 4.11; rs2 Theorem X.12

tests.name: lettering
tests.statement: ambient a = 1, relative b = 1/2, gamma = 0: bound -max(2, 1) = -2; the swapped reading violates relative < 1.

tests.name: scalar
tests.statement: A = lambda >= gamma on C, V = -(a + b|lambda|): A + V >= gamma - (a + b|gamma|), consistent with the bound.

tests.name: relative_one
tests.statement: A = H_0, V = -H_0 (relative bound 1): A + V = 0 on H^2, not closed.

layers.title: The Laplace-Beltrami operator on a Riemannian manifold

targets.name: complexLaplaceBeltrami
targets.statement: For u in C^infinity(X; C), Delta u := -(laplaceBeltrami (Re u) + i laplaceBeltrami (Im u)), the nonnegative Laplacian -div grad; with the Hermitian pairing <dv, du>_g conjugate-linear in v.
hypotheses: X finite-dimensional real smooth manifold, Hausdorff, second countable, boundaryless

api.name: complexLaplaceBeltrami_conj
api.statement: Delta commutes with complex conjugation and is complex-linear.

api.name: complexLaplaceBeltrami_locallyConstant
api.statement: Delta kills locally constant functions.

api.name: complexLaplaceBeltrami_isometry
api.statement: Delta (u o phi) = (Delta u) o phi for a Riemannian isometry phi.

tests.name: flat_sign_gate
tests.statement: Flat R^d: Delta ||x||^2 = -2d (the library operator gives 2d); Delta e^{i<k,x>} = |k|^2 e^{i<k,x>}.

tests.name: hyperbolic
tests.statement: Upper half-plane: Delta y^s = s(1-s) y^s; Delta y = 0, Delta y^2 = -2 y^2.

tests.name: circle
tests.statement: Circle of length 2 pi: Delta e^{in theta} = n^2 e^{in theta}; dropping the conjugation in Green's pairing gives 0 instead of 2 pi n^2.

targets.name: integral_conj_mul_complexLaplaceBeltrami
targets.statement: If u is C^2, v is C^1 and one has compact support, integral conj(v) Delta u dvol_g = integral <dv, du>_g dvol_g; hence Delta is formally symmetric on compactly supported C^2 functions.
hypotheses: X finite-dimensional real smooth manifold, Hausdorff, second countable, boundaryless

targets.name: initialLaplacian
targets.statement: The initial operator Delta_0 : L^2(X) ->l.[C] L^2(X) with domain the image of C_c^infinity(X; C) and action [u] -> [Delta u]; its closure is the minimal operator of bms02 (closure from C_c^infinity), and Delta_0^dagger = (closure Delta_0)^dagger.
hypotheses: X finite-dimensional real smooth manifold, Hausdorff, second countable, boundaryless

locator.where: line 151-157 (S2.1: minimal operator = closure from C_c^infinity, maximal = its adjoint)

api.name: initialLaplacian_dense
api.statement: Delta_0 is densely defined.

api.name: initialLaplacian_symm
api.statement: LinearPMap.IsFormalAdjoint Delta_0 Delta_0.

api.name: inner_initialLaplacian_self
api.statement: <u, Delta_0 u> = integral <du, du>_g >= 0.

api.name: initialLaplacian_isClosable
api.statement: Delta_0 is closable.

tests.name: line
tests.statement: X = R: Delta_0 = -d^2/dx^2 on C_c^infinity, <u, Delta_0 u> = integral |u'|^2.

tests.name: interval
tests.statement: X = (0,1): e^x, e^{-x} in ker(Delta_0^dagger + 1), not essentially self-adjoint.

tests.name: zero_dim
tests.statement: dim X = 0: Delta_0 = 0 on finitely supported functions.

targets.name: maximalLaplacian
targets.statement: Delta_max with domain {u in L^2(X) : the distributional Delta u (K5a transpose action) lies in L^2(X)} and action u -> Delta u.
hypotheses: X finite-dimensional real smooth manifold, Hausdorff, second countable, boundaryless

api.name: maximalLaplacian_smooth
api.statement: On C^2 functions u in L^2 with Delta u in L^2 the action is the classical Delta u.

api.name: maximalLaplacian_regularity
api.statement: dom Delta_max is contained in H^2_loc(X) (K5a interior regularity).

tests.name: abs_exponential
tests.statement: X = R: u = e^{-|x|} has Delta u = -u + 2 delta_0, so u not in dom Delta_max although u in H^1.

tests.name: coulomb
tests.statement: X = R^3: chi/|x| has Delta = 4 pi delta_0 + smooth (Mathlib sign gives -4 pi delta_0); not in dom Delta_max.

tests.name: interval_constant
tests.statement: X = (0,1): 1 in dom Delta_max with Delta_max 1 = 0; e^x in ker(Delta_max + 1).

targets.name: adjoint_initialLaplacian
targets.statement: Delta_0^dagger = Delta_max, and dom Delta_max subset H^2_loc(X).
hypotheses: X finite-dimensional real smooth manifold, Hausdorff, second countable, boundaryless

targets.name: sobolevH1
targets.statement: H^1(X) := {u in L^2(X) : du in L^2(T*X (x) C)} with ||u||^2 + ||du||^2; H^1_0(X) := closure of C_c^infinity(X; C) in H^1(X); energy form a(u,v) := <du, dv>.
hypotheses: X finite-dimensional real smooth manifold, Hausdorff, second countable, boundaryless

api.name: sobolevH1_completeSpace
api.statement: H^1(X) is a Hilbert space and H^1_0(X) a closed subspace, both injectively and densely embedded in L^2(X).

api.name: energyForm_closed
api.statement: a is a closed nonnegative Hermitian form on H^1_0(X) and on H^1(X) (UO-D06).

api.name: energyForm_initial
api.statement: a(u,v) = <u, Delta_0 v> on C_c^infinity.

tests.name: interval
tests.statement: X = (0,1): 1 in H^1 minus H^1_0 (Poincare ||u|| <= ||u'||/pi fails for 1).

tests.name: sesquilinear
tests.statement: a(iu, iu) = a(u,u) and a(u, iv) = i a(u,v): conjugate-linear in the first slot.

targets.name: friedrichsLaplacian
targets.statement: Delta_F := the self-adjoint operator of the closed form a on H^1_0(X) (UO-D06), equal to the Friedrichs extension of Delta_0.
hypotheses: X finite-dimensional real smooth manifold, Hausdorff, second countable, boundaryless

api.name: friedrichsLaplacian_domain
api.statement: dom Delta_F = H^1_0(X) cap dom Delta_max.

api.name: initial_le_friedrichs_le_maximal
api.statement: Delta_0 <= Delta_F <= Delta_max and Delta_F >= 0.

tests.name: interval_dirichlet
tests.statement: X = (0,1): Delta_F is the Dirichlet Laplacian with eigenvalues n^2 pi^2, n >= 1; the form on H^1 gives Neumann with n >= 0.

tests.name: line
tests.statement: X = R: Delta_F = H_0 (d = 1).

tests.name: constant_not_in_domain
tests.statement: X = (0,1): 1 in dom Delta_max but not in dom Delta_F.

targets.name: exists_gaffneyCutoffs
targets.statement: If X is complete (each component complete), there are chi_k in C_c^infinity(X; R) with 0 <= chi_k <= 1, every compact set eventually inside {chi_k = 1}, and sup |grad chi_k| <= 4/k.
hypotheses: X finite-dimensional real smooth manifold, Hausdorff, second countable, boundaryless

tests.name: interval_obstruction
tests.statement: On (0,1) no such sequence exists: 1 <= (4/k)(1/2) fails for k > 2.

tests.name: circles
tests.statement: Countable union of circles: chi_k = 1 on the first k circles, gradient 0.

tests.name: step_thresholds
tests.statement: A smooth step 0 on (-infinity, 1/4], 1 on [3/4, infinity) cannot have |phi'| <= 2 (1 = integral of phi' over (1/4,3/4) <= sup|phi'|/2 forces phi' = 2 there, against phi'(1/4) = 0); thresholds 1/8, 7/8 give average slope 4/3 < 2.

targets.name: essentiallySelfAdjoint_initialLaplacian
targets.statement: If X is complete, Delta_0 is essentially self-adjoint and closure Delta_0 = Delta_F = Delta_max =: Delta_X; H^1_0(X) = H^1(X); dom Delta_X = {u in H^1(X) : Delta u in L^2}; Delta_X >= 0; the form domain is H^1(X) with ||Delta_X^{1/2} u||^2 = ||du||^2; C_c^infinity is an operator core and a form core.
hypotheses: X finite-dimensional real smooth manifold, Hausdorff, second countable, boundaryless

locator.where: line 245-246 (Corollary 2.10), 252-256 (Remark 2.12), 128-129 (M connected; the disconnected case componentwise); strichartz83 Theorem 2.4; chernoff73; gaffney54

tests.name: flat
tests.statement: Flat R^d: Delta_X = H_0 with domain H^2.

tests.name: punctured_R4
tests.statement: R^4 minus {0}: incomplete but essentially self-adjoint (rs2 SX.1), so completeness is not necessary.

tests.name: interval
tests.statement: (0,1): incomplete, not essentially self-adjoint, Delta_F /= Delta_max.

targets.name: laplacianEigenvalue
targets.statement: For complete X: lambda_0(X) := lambda_0(Delta_X) (X nonempty); lambda_k(X) := mu_{k+1}(Delta_X) of 1.6a; lambda_1^+(X) := inf (sigma(Delta_X) minus {0}) in [0, infinity].

api.name: laplacianEigenvalue_zero_eq_inf
api.statement: lambda_0(X) = inf of integral <du,du>_g / integral |u|^2 over nonzero u in C_c^infinity.

api.name: laplacianEigenvalue_eq
api.statement: lambda_k(X) are the eigenvalues below inf sigma_ess(Delta_X) with multiplicity, then inf sigma_ess.

api.name: firstPositive_eq
api.statement: For connected X of finite volume with 0 isolated in sigma(Delta_X), lambda_1^+(X) = lambda_1(X).

tests.name: circle

tests.statement: X = R: lambda_0 = 0 not an eigenvalue, lambda_1^+ = 0 = lambda_1.

tests.name: point_torus

targets.name: ker_laplacian
targets.statement: For complete X, ker Delta_X = {u in L^2(X) locally constant a.e.}; its dimension is the number of components of finite volume; on connected X, 0 is an eigenvalue iff vol_g(X) < infinity, and then it is simple.
hypotheses: X finite-dimensional real smooth manifold, Hausdorff, second countable, boundaryless

targets.name: compact_laplacian_spectrum
targets.statement: For compact X, Delta_X is K5a's H^2 realisation of the nonnegative scalar Hodge Laplacian, with compact resolvent; sigma(Delta_X) = sigma_disc(Delta_X), every spectral value is an eigenvalue of finite multiplicity, and L^2(X) has an orthonormal basis of smooth eigenfunctions; mult(0) = number of components. If X is nonempty, the eigenvalues with multiplicity are 0 = lambda_0 <= lambda_1 <= ... with lambda_k = lambda_k(X) of 3.7a, and for k < dim L^2(X) (every k when dim X >= 1) lambda_k = rayleighMinMax top k of VariationalMethods 4.4 for the compact form pair (H^1(X) -> L^2(X), a) of 3.4. If dim X >= 1 and X nonempty, every lambda_k is finite and lambda_k -> infinity.
hypotheses: X finite-dimensional real smooth manifold, Hausdorff, second countable, boundaryless

tests.name: sphere
tests.statement: Round S^2: eigenvalues l(l+1) with multiplicity 2l+1.

tests.name: zero_dim
tests.statement: A finite set of N >= 1 points: L^2 = C^N, Delta_X = 0, lambda_0 = ... = lambda_{N-1} = 0 and lambda_k = +infinity for k >= N (1.6a), whereas rayleighMinMax top k = 0 for k >= N is VariationalMethods' junk value: the identification is asserted for k < N only, and the unboundedness clause fails (all finite eigenvalues are 0), so it needs dim X >= 1.

tests.name: two_circles
tests.statement: Two disjoint circles: 0 has multiplicity 2.

tests.name: empty
tests.statement: X = empty is compact with L^2 = 0 and sigma(Delta_X) = empty: no eigenvalue lambda_0 = 0, lambda_0(X) = mu_1 = +infinity; the eigenvalue clause is stated for nonempty X.

targets.name: laplacian_add_boundedPotential
targets.statement: For complete X and real V in L^infinity(X): Delta_X + V is self-adjoint on dom Delta_X, Delta_0 + V is essentially self-adjoint on C_c^infinity with closure Delta_X + V, Delta_X + V >= ess inf V; for compact X it has compact resolvent.
hypotheses: X finite-dimensional real smooth manifold, Hausdorff, second countable, boundaryless

tests.name: constant
